newsitem.title: USA: U.S. mulls logistical aid in Zaire crisis.
newsitem.headline: U.S. mulls logistical aid in Zaire crisis.

text.p: The United States is considering providing logistical support to help meet refugee needs in Zaire but not military ground troops, senior officials said on Wednesday.

"There have been a number of proposals made...and we're looking at all of them. Some of the proposals would require logistical support by the United States Armed Forces. We're not talking about ground force units here (but) logistical support. And we're looking at that question," State Department spokesman Nicholas Burns said.

Another senior official stressed that no decision had been made about what, if any, role Washington would play and said there was "healthy scepticism" in the Clinton administration about the proposed use of troops.
"Troops are not even the leading option at this point," he said, adding: "We would only consider logistical support."

Proposals advanced in recent days include a call for the international community to establish a security force on the ground to guarantee the safety of refugees fleeing border fighting between Zairean army troops and rebel forces.
Some 1.1 million refugees, lacking water, food and medicine, are said to be at risk and fleeing into Zaire's interior. Most fled Rwanda after the genocide of 1994.
